subject: Re: BYOK witness automation & egress bastion — next steps
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@acme-health.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: BYOK witness automation & egress bastion — initial proposal

Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a compact plan to support Acme Health's request for a hardened BYOK (bring-your-own-key) handoff for Redwood Private instances inside your VPC. The two things you asked we clarify were: (1) how an automated "witness" (ephemeral key witness/attestation) can participate in the ceremony without requiring permanent operator access, and (2) how the egress/bastion path will be constrained when the HSM-to-operator flow needs to be exercised for recovery/rotation.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Witness automation: a short-lived, ephemeral witness process runs inside a dedicated maintenance subnet in customer VPC. It performs attestations against the HSM and posts signed receipts to a customer-owned audit bucket. It never stores unwrapped key material.
- Operator separation: operators authenticate via short-lived certs (ACME-managed PKI). Operator consoles must use the bastion jump host which only allows SSH/HTTPS to the HSM management VLAN; no broad egress is permitted.
- Rotation & rollback: rotation is staged into canary tenants; automatic failover uses pre-published fallback key-wrapping policy.

Open items we need from Acme before we schedule the ceremony:
1) Confirm whether Acme wants the witness to be run as a customer-managed Lambda/container (we recommend container) or Redwood-managed ephemeral instance.
2) Confirm the CIDR ranges we can use for the maintenance subnet and the bastion public IP(s) for allow-listing in the HSM firewall.
3) Your preferred SLO for rotation (e.g., 24h target vs. 72h) so we can size the automation retries.

I'm looping in our security lead (Naomi) and the platform engineer (Soojin) for nitty-gritty details. If that summary looks good, we'll schedule a short 30 min pre-ceremony tech review and a separate dry-run with your ops team.

Attachments: runbook_byo_witness_v2.pdf (draft runbook), egress_bastion_network_diagram.png (network sketch)

Best,
Michael Grant
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@acme-health.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK witness automation & egress bastion — initial proposal

Michael / Sam —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few security clarifications from our side before we lock the plan:

1) Evidence model: the witness process will produce two artifacts per ceremony: a signed-attestation blob (non-sensitive, contains HSM attestation quotes and metadata) and a transaction receipt (signed, includes key version and wrap-policy id). We need to confirm retention requirements for the audit bucket (we propose immutable objects with 90d retention default).

2) HSM access policy: ensure the HSM management VLAN only accepts connections from the bastion's static egress IP(s). For emergency key-recovery, we'll require an out-of-band approval flow (DocuSign + 2 on-call confirmations).

3) Ephemeral creds and PKI: If Acme elects Redwood-managed witness instances, we will issue short-lived certs (max 1 hour lifetime). For customer-managed containers, we need a CSR and ACME's PKI root fingerprint.

4) Test plan: request a staged dry-run that exercises both the happy-path rotation and a simulated operator-eviction (to ensure the witness proves control without key exposure). For the eviction scenario we will use test keys only.

Can you confirm the bucket location (us-west-2 vs us-east-1) and the preferred retention? I note Sam mentioned a preference for keeping audit artifacts inside Acme's cloud tenancy — that works, and reduces egress risk.

Naomi
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment requests: please provide the proposed bastion egress IP(s) and the CSR if ACME manages PKI.

From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@acme-health.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Security Team <security@acme-health.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK witness automation & egress bastion — initial proposal

Thanks — this looks good and aligns with our internal compliance. Quick answers:

- We want the witness run inside our tenancy (customer-managed container) so Acme maintains the provenance chain. We'll provide a CSR and the PKI details by EOD Monday.
- Audit bucket: keep artifacts inside our account in us-east-1 with 180d retention and object-lock enabled.
- Bastion IPs: we'll reserve two static public IPs for allow-listing; I'll send the allocation in a follow-up email.
- Rotation SLO: 48 hours for full rotation (acceptable for our Ops team).

Two asks on scheduling:
1) Can Redwood run the dry-run with our ops on Thursday 26 Aug at 10:00 ET?
2) We want to include our procurement contact on the final schedule to confirm access windows and any procurement approvals that may be needed for temporary operator certs.

If you need me to open a Jira with the acceptance criteria, tell me which template to use and I'll add it.

—Sam
Head of Cloud Security, Acme Health

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@acme-health.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK witness automation & egress bastion — scheduling and playbook

Sam / team —

Great, thanks for the quick answers and the retention guidance. Thursday 26 Aug 10:00 ET works for the dry-run — I've booked a 45-minute slot on our side and invited an engineer who will run the witness automation. Please expect separate invites for the procurement stake-holders.

I've attached a trimmed playbook (witness_automation_playbook.sh) that outlines the automation steps we run during the dry-run (it is a runnable script with clear NO-OP switches to avoid live key wrapping). The runbook_byo_witness_v2.pdf includes the evacuation/eviction sequence we will test.

Quick operational notes:
- For the dry-run, we'll only use test HSM partitions and test wrap-keys with clear metadata that denotes 'TEST'.
- During the operator-eviction scenario we'll enforce the out-of-band DocuSign approval; please confirm the two approvers' names for the dry-run (we'll need them in the script).
- I'll coordinate with Ben on network connectivity checks; Ben will reach out with a small connectivity test script to validate the bastion egress and HSM firewall rules ahead of the dry-run.

Next steps (from Redwood):
1) Soojin to share the playbook/script (attached).
2) Ben to run connectivity checks and post results to the shared Drive link.
3) Michael to host the pre-ceremony tech review (15 min) on Wednesday 25 Aug 09:30 ET.

Attachments: witness_automation_playbook.sh (script stub, NO-OP by default), runbook_byo_witness_v2.pdf (draft)

Thanks — looking forward to the dry-run.

—Soojin Lee
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
